clue.text: Interfered, making a point about motorway

indicators.note: about means placed around, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: something tapered narrows to a point
M is the standard abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Someone meddled while building the sharp end of a new motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: TAPERED goes about M to give TAMPERED.
explanation.definitionFit: To tamper with something is to meddle or interfere with it without permission.

clue.text: Prosper from the endless, endless water supply

indicators.note: each endless tells us to drop the final letter of the word that follows it

blocks.note: taken as written, then cut short
a river supplies water, then cut short

explanation.surface: A town grows rich from an inexhaustible water source.
explanation.walkthrough: THE loses its E and RIVER its R, leaving TH + RIVE = THRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrive is to flourish and do well, a direct synonym for prospering.

clue.text: Parent joins offspring in secret society

definitions.note: the answer names the society's members

blocks.note: ma is an informal word for mother
sons are male offspring

explanation.surface: A father and his children both join a clandestine brotherhood.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons, often called Masons, form a fraternal order famous for its secret rituals and handshakes.

clue.text: In time, traitor will make mistakes

indicators.note: one word placed in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who betrays their side

explanation.surface: Given long enough, a turncoat will slip up.
explanation.walkthrough: In time looks like 'eventually', but it tells you where to put the traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for printing or writing errors, often listed on a correction slip.

clue.text: Heights taken from architectural drawings

blocks.note: first meaning: altitudes above a level
second meaning: flat drawings of a building's faces

explanation.surface: Measurements of how tall something is are read off the blueprints.
explanation.definitionFit: Elevation means altitude, and in architecture it is also a drawing of one face of a building seen straight on.

clue.text: Loosens trousers

blocks.note: first meaning: makes less taut
second meaning: casual pairs of pants

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like someone easing their waistband; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To slack a rope is to ease its tension, and slacks are loose casual trousers.

clue.text: Chemical plant?

blocks.note: surface reading: a factory making chemicals
setter's reading: a growing plant named after a chemical compound, quicklime

explanation.walkthrough: Plant means a factory in the surface but a living tree in the answer, and lime is calcium oxide as well as a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The linden is a tree whose common name is shared with the caustic substance calcium oxide.

clue.text: Giving fresh start to prisoner makes a real difference

indicators.note: a fresh version is a new arrangement, so these letters are reworked

blocks.note: con is short for convict
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Offering an inmate a new beginning changes their life completely.
explanation.walkthrough: Fresh start sounds like a second chance; here only start is reworked and prisoner comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A contrast is a marked distinction between things set side by side.

clue.text: Anxious feeling takes us over poet ending prematurely

indicators.note: stopping early means the poet's name loses its final letter
to take something in is to hold it inside

blocks.note: Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nerves strike us when a poet's reading is cut off early.
explanation.walkthrough: Spenser loses its R, and the shortened name takes US after its first letter. Over is just placement in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Suspense is the tense, uncertain anxiety of waiting to find out what happens.

clue.text: Takes top off jam and puts aside for later

indicators.note: removing the top of a word drops its first letter

blocks.note: preserves are jams and fruit spreads

explanation.surface: Someone opens a jar of jam and saves it for another day.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve something is to keep it back for future use.

clue.text: Changes compensation

blocks.note: first meaning: alters or revises, as with a text
second meaning: recompense, as in making the answer

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about altering a payout; the words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Amend is a verb for revising a law or text, and amends is a plural noun meaning reparation for a wrong.

clue.text: A blind Italian

blocks.note: first meaning: a window blind of horizontal slats
second meaning: a native of a city in northern Italy

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an Italian person who cannot see; blind is actually the window covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian blind has adjustable horizontal slats, and a Venetian is someone from Venice in Italy.

clue.text: Lack food when harvest fails to start and is disrupted

indicators.note: not getting going means the word loses its first letter
disrupting something throws it out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People go hungry when the crops fail.
explanation.walkthrough: Harvest drops its H, and the remaining letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To starve is to suffer severely from having nothing to eat.

clue.text: One's position in society has improved - and is rising

blocks.note: standing is status or reputation
things that have improved are said to be up

explanation.surface: A social climber's status is getting better and still climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing up means getting to one's feet, the same as rising from a seat.

clue.text: Highly skilled lovers?

definitions.note: adjective in the clue; the answer names women who are highly skilled

blocks.note: first meaning: women who have mastered an art, as in a mistress of her craft
second meaning: women having affairs with married men

explanation.surface: Expert romantic partners are being praised.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the two senses are being run together.
explanation.definitionFit: The feminine of master means a woman expert in a field, and also a woman in an extramarital affair.

clue.text: Fights break out when the French get into scrapes

indicators.note: getting into something means going inside it

blocks.note: a scuff is a scrape on a surface
le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: Brawls erupt when French people find themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrapes looks like trouble or tight spots, but it means scratch marks here.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuffles are short, confused tussles, a mild kind of fight.

clue.text: Include it in clever caption

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside

blocks.note: subtle means shrewd and clever
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to slip a witty line into a picture caption.
explanation.definitionFit: A subtitle is a caption, especially text shown at the bottom of a film screen.

clue.text: Fasten untidy file with strap as a safeguard

indicators.note: something untidy is in disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
to belt is to fasten with a belt

explanation.surface: Someone straps up a messy dossier to keep it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: With lets BELT join the rearranged letters in either order.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifebelt is a buoyant belt or ring worn to keep a person afloat in water, a protective strap.

clue.text: Warning to take care before mixing gin

indicators.note: mixing stirs the letters into a new order

blocks.note: caution is care taken to avoid danger
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to be careful before making a gin cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cautioning someone is giving them a warning, as police do before an arrest.

clue.text: Store up one''s courage

blocks.note: first meaning: keep in, as in bottling up feelings
second meaning: British slang for nerve

explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, bottle means nerve, as in 'he lost his bottle'.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle up emotion is to hold it in, and bottle is informal British for daring or nerve.

clue.text: Person responsible for making cuts at work?

definitions.text: Person responsible for making cuts at work?

blocks.clueFragment: Person responsible for making cuts at work?
blocks.note: surface reading: a manager who reduces budgets or jobs

blocks.clueFragment: Person responsible for making cuts at work?
blocks.note: setter's reading: someone who trims text or film as their job

explanation.walkthrough: Cuts suggests redundancies, but the job meant is trimming copy or footage.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor shortens and revises written or filmed material, removing unwanted parts.

clue.text: Removed all trace of Times editor

blocks.note: eras are periods of time
ed is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor was wiped from the record.
explanation.walkthrough: Times looks like The Times newspaper but is a plain plural.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to rub out or delete something so nothing remains.

clue.text: A mechanic would be more suitable

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who assembles machinery
second meaning: comparative of fit

explanation.surface: Hiring a trained engineer would be a better choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A fitter assembles or installs parts, and fitter is also the comparative adjective meaning better suited.

clue.text: Chaos results from woman's rule

blocks.note: Di is a woman's name, so woman's is Di's
an order is a rule or command

explanation.surface: Anarchy follows when a woman takes charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Disorder is a state of confusion and lack of organisation, much like chaos.

clue.text: Make a mess, like young animals

blocks.note: first meaning: scatter rubbish
second meaning: a brood born at one time

explanation.surface: Someone is as untidy as a pack of puppies.
explanation.definitionFit: To litter is to drop rubbish carelessly, and a litter is a group of animals born together.

clue.text: Disturbs a foreign serviceman with display of bad taste)

indicators.note: something bad is spoilt or wrong, so the letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written
a GI is an American soldier, foreign from a British view
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An overseas soldier's boorish behaviour upsets the locals.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray closing bracket is in the published clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate is to stir up, upset or trouble someone.

clue.text: Covers in bits of paper

blocks.note: first meaning: bedclothes
second meaning: single pages

explanation.surface: Something is wrapped up in scraps of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets are the linen that covers a bed, and also individual pieces of paper.

clue.text: Seemed secretary returned and looked, they say

indicators.note: something returned comes back the other way
they say means we go by how the word is spoken

blocks.note: PA stands for personal assistant
peered means looked closely

explanation.surface: An assistant came back and glanced around, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeared can mean gave the impression of being, the same sense as seemed.
